Case name: American Trucking Associations, Inc. v. City of Los Angeles
Court: Supreme Court of the United States
One-sentence holding: Municipal port concession agreements mandating designated truck routes and parking plans have the force and effect of law and are preempted by the Federal Aviation Administration Authorization Act.

Case name: City of Lafayette v. County of Contra Costa
Court: California Court of Appeal, First District
One-sentence holding: Section 21101 does not authorize a city to close a street or divert traffic away from its boundaries onto an adjoining jurisdiction without express statutory authority.
Local authorities may not close streets or divert vehicular traffic through physical barriers unless specifically authorized by the Legislature under Section 21101.

Case name: City of Poway v. City of San Diego
Court: California Court of Appeal, Fourth District
One-sentence holding: A city may not close a public road that provides access between jurisdictions or divert commuter traffic under Section 21101 where doing so impairs regional circulation and regional general plan consistency.

Case name: Save the Sunset Strip Coalition v. City of West Hollywood
Court: California Court of Appeal, Second District
One-sentence holding: Municipalities possess police power under Section 21101 to alter traffic circulation and turn restrictions without violating regional traffic rights if grounded in safety findings.

Case name: Citizens for Improved Sorrento Access, Inc. v. City of San Diego
Court: California Court of Appeal, Fourth District
One-sentence holding: Vehicle Code section 21101, subdivision (f), authorizes local authorities to prohibit entry to, or exit from, any street by vehicles to implement local traffic management plans.

Case name: Neary v. Town of Los Altos Hills
Court: California Court of Appeal, First District
One-sentence holding: An ordinance prohibiting commercial vehicles exceeding a designated gross weight limit on town streets is valid under Section 35701 when alternate routes are available.

Case name: National Tank Truck Carriers, Inc. v. City of New York
Court: United States Court of Appeals, Second Circuit
Provision addressed: Hazardous Materials Transportation Act (49 U.S.C. § 5112) / HM-164
One-sentence holding: City routing regulations restricting hazardous material transport across bridges and during daytime hours were not preempted where adequate alternative routing exists.

Case name: State of New Jersey v. Borough of Leonia
Court: Superior Court of New Jersey, Law Division, Bergen County
One-sentence holding: Municipalities lack statutory authority under Title 39 to close public municipal streets to all non-residents without prior written approval of the Commissioner of Transportation, invalidating Leonia's blanket rush-hour permit closures enacted in response to Waze.

Court: Supreme Court of the United States
Provision addressed: U.S. Const. art. I, § 8, cl. 3 (Dormant Commerce Clause)
One-sentence holding: State route and vehicle length limitations that severely burden interstate freight while providing marginal local safety benefits violate the Dormant Commerce Clause.
